image.name: Amwaste LLC
image.subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling
image.description: Amwaste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, landfill, and recycling services in the Southeastern United States. Its customer base includes residential, commercial, construction and industrial end markets across Alabama, Georgia, and Louisiana. The business operates an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by owned disposal sites, transfer stations, and recycling infrastructure. Public materials describe a platform with more than 300,000 customers, eight landfill sites, ten transfer stations, and a materials recovery facility. The company has expanded through bolt-on acquisitions and local contract wins to deepen density in its core Southeastern markets. 3i invested growth capital through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in July 2023, and current ownership percentages are not publicly disclosed.

image.name: EC Waste
image.subsector: Solid waste collection, transfer, and landfill services
image.description: EC Waste provides non-hazardous solid waste collection, transfer, recycling, and disposal services across Puerto Rico. Its customers include residential, commercial, industrial, and municipal accounts served through an island-wide operating footprint. The business uses an asset-heavy, vertically integrated model supported by disposal sites, transfer infrastructure, hauling operations, and related environmental services. 3i has described the company as the largest vertically integrated waste-services provider in Puerto Rico, with more than 80,000 customers and multiple disposal and transfer assets. The platform has grown through acquisitions, including the 2020 purchase of Republic Services of Puerto Rico and the 2025 acquisition of ARB Waste Services. 3i acquired a majority interest through the 3i North American Infrastructure Fund in 2021, with management reinvesting alongside the fund.

image.name: Regional Rail, LLC
image.description: Regional Rail owns and operates short-line freight railroads and related rail services across the United States and Canada. Its customer base spans industrial, agricultural, chemicals, aggregates, food, and logistics end markets that depend on local freight connectivity and transload services. The company follows an asset-heavy operating model built around owned and leased track, rail-served industrial infrastructure, and operating railroad franchises. Public disclosures describe a network of more than 875 route miles, 17 railroad operations, and approximately 65,000 annual carloads as of 2023. The footprint expanded materially after 2019 through acquisitions in Florida, the Midwest, Ohio, Indiana, and western Canada. 3i invested in Regional Rail in July 2019 as its North American rail infrastructure platform and remains the disclosed owner.

image.name: Durham Region Courthouse
image.description: Durham Region Courthouse is an operational judicial public-private partnership in Oshawa, Ontario. Access Justice Durham Limited is responsible for the financing, maintenance and lifecycle renewal of the approximately 440,000-square-foot courthouse, which consolidates Superior Court and Ontario Court of Justice services in 33 courtrooms. Babcock & Brown Public Partnerships, INPP's predecessor, acquired 100% of the project-company equity at financial close in March 2007. INPP and Amber currently report 100% equity ownership and a 30-year term from construction completion; Infrastructure Ontario records construction completion in November 2009.

milestones.event: The project received an Award of Merit for Project Financing from the Canadian Council for Public-Private Partnerships.
Babcock & Brown Public Partnerships, INPP's predecessor, acquired 100% of Access Justice Durham Limited at financial close.

image.name: Chief Power
image.description: Chief Power is an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund V-backed merchant-generation platform holding partial tenant-in-common interests in the Keystone and Conemaugh coal-fired generating stations in western Pennsylvania. ArcLight established the platform in 2014 and expanded it through a separately financed acquisition in 2019. After a 2020 lender restructuring transferred control of the original tranche, Fund V retained a small minority voting interest and continued to control the separately owned Chief Power Finance II tranche. Current public filings identify Fund V as holding greater than 10% voting interests in each II plant-owner entity, while the exact Fund V economic percentage is not publicly disclosed. Chief Power is the single PortCo; its financing entities, transfer parent, plant-owner subsidiaries and the two jointly owned generating stations are not separate portfolio companies.

image.name: Orca Acquisitions, LLC
image.subsector: Merchant power generation and industrial steam
image.description: Orca Acquisitions, LLC is an ArcLight Energy Partners Fund VI and Olympus Power joint-venture platform that indirectly owns Walleye Power, LLC through Walleye Energy Holdings, LLC. Walleye owns and operates the Bay Shore merchant-power and industrial-steam facility in Oregon, Ohio. A June 2026 FERC filing reports 136 MW of summer-rated steam generation and a 16 MW oil-fired unit. ArcLight Orca Holdings, LLC holds 95% of Orca's Class A managing interests, appoints two management-committee members and controls day-to-day decisions. Olympus affiliates hold the remaining 5% of Class A interests and all non-managing, non-voting Class B interests. The exact overall economic ownership split is not publicly disclosed. Orca is the single PortCo; Walleye, its holding company, Bay Shore and the individual generating units are subsidiaries or assets beneath the platform. No Orca-specific sale or pending ownership transfer was identified through August 14, 2026.

image.description: TransMontaigne Partners LLC is a Denver-based U.S. midstream infrastructure platform providing terminaling, storage, transportation, blending and related logistics for refined petroleum products, renewable fuels and feedstocks, crude oil, chemicals, fertilizers and other bulk liquids. image.name: Rover Pipeline
image.description: Rover Pipeline LLC is a large-scale interstate natural gas transmission system connecting Marcellus and Utica production in Pennsylvania and West Virginia with demand markets across Ohio, Michigan and the broader Midwest. The approximately 700-to-713-mile system has 3.425 Bcf/d of transportation capacity, is substantially contracted under long-term agreements and is operated by an Energy Transfer affiliate. The canonical PortCo is Rover Pipeline LLC; ET Rover Pipeline LLC, BCP Renaissance entities and Traverse Midstream Partners are ownership vehicles, while pipeline segments, interconnects and the separately owned Ohio River System are outside the Rover company boundary. Ares Management owns a 32.4% indirect interest through Ares Core Infrastructure Fund and the BCP Renaissance vehicles, Energy Transfer reports a 32.6% economic interest through ET Rover Pipeline LLC, and ePointZero owns 35% through Traverse. Blackstone's 32.44% indirect interest was realized when Ares acquired its vehicles on April 28, 2026. Rover's separately attributable headquarters, founding year and Energy Transfer's precise initial investment date are not publicly disclosed. No later Rover-level sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

image.name: Virginia International Gateway
image.description: Virginia International Gateway is the private owner of the highly automated VIG marine container terminal in Portsmouth, Virginia. The terminal handles containerized cargo for ocean carriers, beneficial cargo owners, railroads, motor carriers and regional supply chains; Astatine describes approximately 2 million TEU of annual throughput capacity. Virginia International Gateway, Inc. owns the terminal, the Virginia Port Authority leases it under a long-term facilities lease, and the authority's Virginia International Terminals subsidiary operates it. The facility opened in 2007 as APM Terminals Virginia. Affiliates of Alinda-managed funds and USS acquired it in August 2014 and renamed it VIG. Astatine now lists one VIG profile as Active and a separate Fund II investment as exited in 2019. The Virginia Port Authority's August 2025 final official statement identifies USS and PSP as the current underlying owners, supporting an active Astatine manager attribution and an active PSP direct-owner association while preserving the realized Fund II period. The active Astatine fund or managed-account vehicle, manager-level stake and entry date, plus PSP's entry date and percentage, are not publicly disclosed. No later full sale, signed pending exit or transfer of terminal title to the port authority was identified through August 18, 2026. APM Terminals Virginia is the predecessor name; VPA, VIT, lease interests, bonds, cranes and expansion projects are not separate PortCos.
